answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission. Each identity must submit a minimum of 12 timed interactions before earning economic privileges, with inter-arrival variance checked against a sonnet-like cadence profile; bursts or metronomic spacing flag the identity as synthetic and reset its clock. An attacker must then sustain the pattern across an island of many identities, since a lone vertex in the traffic graph is trivially filtered. Cost: roughly 12x the compute and latency budget per fake identity, plus continuous scheduling overhead while real agents pay nothing extra.
